headlines.title: Trump says AI doesn’t need guardrails, only a ‘high IQ’ president
headlines.description: He also alleged the existence of a “sick conspiracy” against AI and data centers, at a time when Americans are increasingly concerned about the technology.

headlines.title: China dismisses AI slowdown calls and blasts ‘fearmongering’ from U.S. tech leaders
headlines.description: Urgent calls for a slowdown in the development of artificial intelligence may cite a grave threat to humanity, but China says the warnings are instead aimed at slowing its progress as America’s rival superpower.

headlines.title: Obama says Democrats should have a ‘very clear plan’ on AI policy
headlines.description: Researchers at AI companies have been warning about safety risks, and industry leaders have called for a slowdown in development.

headlines.title: Anthropic whistleblower says Congress should let AI companies regulate themselves for now
headlines.description: Former AI researcher Jacob Coxon said any laws Congress passes to regulate the technology need to be able to respond to newly created models quickly.

headlines.title: Stocks slip, but traders largely shake off warnings that AI industry should slow down
headlines.description: Stocks tumbled Monday, led by tech stocks, after leading artificial intelligence CEOs said the pace of developing the revolutionary technology should slow down.

headlines.title: Trump downplays need for guardrails on artificial intelligence
headlines.description: In a post on social media, President Trump downplayed the need for regulatory guardrails on artificial intelligence, instead saying a "high IQ" president is enough to oversee it. NBC News' Gabe Gutierrez and Jonathan Allen report on the calls for lawmakers to get involved on AI regulations.

headlines.title: Mitch McConnell returns to the Senate after three-month absence
headlines.description: Sen. Mitch McConnell, R-Ky., returned to the Senate on Monday after a more than three-month absence.

headlines.title: Pentagon inspector general says Iran war has led to a shortfall of U.S. munitions
headlines.description: It’s the first public report on the ongoing war started Feb. 28 by the U.S. and Israel.

headlines.title: Report finds 'Alligator Alcatraz' held immigrants in cages the size of phone booths
headlines.description: A report from the Department of Homeland Security’s inspector general found that some immigrants detained at the now-shuttered "Alligator Alcatraz" were at times confined to cages roughly the size of a phone booth. NBC News' Julia Ainsley has details on the report's findings.

headlines.title: Macklemore says he was dropped from Ed Sheeran tour after Robert Kraft organized boycott
headlines.description: Macklemore has been dropped from Ed Sheeran’s tour after he says New England Patriots owner Robert Kraft organized a boycott among stadium owners over the rapper’s remarks in support of Palestinians.

headlines.title: Top AI Developers Warn the Technology is Developing Too Rapidly
headlines.description: Some of the world’s leading creators of AI are uniting in warning of the dangers of the technology advancing too quickly and publicly calling for a slowdown. They say that it could, in the not-too-distant future, actually outsmart the researchers who are building it and pose an existential threat to humanity. NBC’s Christine Romans reports and Josh Tyrangiel, staff writer at The Atlantic and author of "AI for Good: How Real People Are Using Artificial Intelligence to Fix Things That Matter,"

headlines.title: Chinese company releases video of humanoid robot walking off assembly line on its own
headlines.description: Chinese company Xpeng released a video showing its new humanoid robot IRON walking off the assembly line on its own. It’s the latest step in the robot arms race between the U.S. and China that could eventually lead to mass production of the humanoids. NBC News’ Priscilla Thompson reports.
